correctness.rationale: The claim is reduced exactly to forbidding three binary words when one lies on a Hamming geodesic between the other two. Translation normalizes an arbitrary nonempty code to contain the zero word. The bundled depth-first search is exhaustive by an induction on its candidate mask: it removes exactly those future vertices that would create a forbidden triple with two already selected vertices. It finds 7,560 normalized nine-word codes and zero normalized ten-word codes. A direct replay of the defining triple condition is applied to every maximum. The 107,520 labeled count follows from a free translation action on an odd nine-set, and the two full isometry orbits are reconstructed explicitly from all translations and all \(7!\) coordinate permutations.
risks: The classification is finite and computer-assisted; a coding error is the principal correctness risk. It is mitigated by deriving forbidden triples directly from the defining geodesic condition, separately rerunning the defining condition on every maximum, checking target size ten exhaustively, and rebuilding the symmetry orbits from generators without relying on stored orbit labels.

value.rationale: The dimension-seven optimum is a natural benchmark: it is the last hypercube dimension whose exact cardinality was known before the recently closed dimension-eight case. A complete equality classification supplies substantially more structure than the known number 9: it counts every labeled optimum, proves there are exactly two natural geometries, gives their stabilizers, and separates them by simple intrinsic distance and coordinate profiles. Such equality information is useful for understanding extremal constructions and for testing structural conjectures in separating/frameproof code theory.
risks: The result is a finite classification and does not itself yield a new asymptotic bound or higher-dimensional construction; its value rests on being a complete structural refinement of a standard exact benchmark rather than on downstream generality.
